narrative: An Apple vehicle, operating in manual mode and stopped at a stop sign in the Main Street Cupertino retail center parking lot, was struck on the left rear bumper by a diagonally-parked Subaru reversing out of a parking space at low speed. Both vehicles sustained minor damage. At the time of the incident, no injuries were reported by either party and law enforcement was not called to the scene.

An Argo AI Autonomous Vehicle ("Argo AV") was impacted by a cyclist while traveling east on Park Ave and approaching Cambridge Ave. The Argo AV was traveling in its lane adjacent to a cyclist who was traveling in a marked bike lane. As the Argo AV was passing the cyclist (while maintaining more than 2 meters of lateral margin), the cyclist veered left into the Argo AV's lane. In response, the Argo AV steered away from the cyclist, but the cyclist continued into the lane and the bicycle's left handlebar made contact with the Argo AV's passenger side door handle. The Test Specialist brought the AV to a stop. The cyclist maintained balance, continued to cross the lanes behind the stopped Argo AV, and left the scene after a brief conversation with the left seat Test Specialist, during which the cyclist indicated that he was fine and apologized. The Argo AV sustained minor damage to its passenger side door handle.

A Cruise autonomous vehicle (“Cruise AV”), operating in driverless autonomous mode, was traveling northbound on Harrison St. between 18th Street and 19th Street. As the Cruise AV was coming to a stop for a stop sign at the intersection with 18th Street, a van approaching from the rear failed to stop behind the Cruise AV and made contact with the Cruise AV's rear bumper, damaging the rear bumper of the Cruise AV. Police and Emergency Medical Services were called and the Cruise AV was towed from the scene. The driver of the van was transported by Emergency Medical Services for further evaluation.

A Cruise autonomous vehicle (“Cruise AV”), operating in supervised autonomous mode, was traveling southbound on Selby Street between Palou Avenue and Oakdale Avenue. The Cruise AV came to a stop behind a semi-trailer truck that was slowly reversing diagonally onto Selby Street from the intersection with Palou Avenue. As the semi-trailer truck began encroaching into the Cruise AV’s lane of travel, the Cruise AV operator disengaged from autonomous into manual mode and began reversing the Cruise AV, causing the Cruise AV to back into a different semi-trailer truck parked behind the Cruise AV. This caused damage to the Cruise AV’s rear passenger side wheel molding. The Cruise AV operator left information for the other party and there were no reported injuries.

A Cruise autonomous vehicle ("AV"), operating in driverless autonomous mode, was at a complete stop in response to a red light on eastbound Bush Street in the second leftmost lane at the intersection with Sansome Street. As the AV attempted to maneuver into the left turn lane, the AV slowed to a complete stop. A delivery truck traveling behind and to the left of the AV proceeded forward and attempted to drive past the AV on the left. Shortly thereafter, the delivery truck made contact with the AV, damaging the AV’s front driver side bumper fascia and front driver side wheel opening molding. The driver of the delivery truck left the scene without exchanging information. There were no reported injuries.

A Cruise autonomous vehicle ("AV"), operating in manual mode, was traveling northbound on 25th Avenue between California Street and Clement Street. The AV operator improperly engaged from manual into autonomous mode while the AV was in motion, temporarily causing the AV to steer to the right. The AV operator then disengaged from autonomous mode into manual mode, and shortly thereafter, the AV made contact with an unoccupied and parked red Chrysler Voyager. This caused damage to the AV’s front passenger side bumper fascia. The AV operator left contact information for the other party and there were no reported injuries.

A Cruise autonomous vehicle ("Cruise AV"), operating in driverless autonomous mode, was at a complete stop in response to a red light on southbound Masonic Avenue at the intersection with Oak Street. At the intersection, an Acura Sedan was stopped in front of the Cruise AV in the left southbound lane. To the right of the Cruise AV, was a BMW Sedan in the right southbound lane. In response to the green light, the Acura Sedan made a signaled left turn onto Oak Street as the BMW Sedan stayed parallel to the Cruise AV. As the Cruise AV entered the intersection, the BMW Sedan made a prohibited left turn from the right southbound lane on Masonic Avenue with no turn signal. The Cruise AV braked and, shortly thereafter, the BMW Sedan made contact with the Cruise AV, damaging the front right bumper of the Cruise AV. The driver of the BMW Sedan left the scene without exchanging information. There were no injuries and Cruise filed a police report on February 12, 2022.

A Cruise autonomous vehicle (“Cruise AV”), operating in autonomous mode, was traveling southeast bound on 11th Street between Howard and Folsom Streets when the Cruise AV slowed down for a passing motorcyclist behind it. The driver of the Cruise AV disengaged from autonomous mode and, shortly thereafter, the motorcyclist made contact with the left rear corner of the Cruise AV. The collision resulted in damage to both the Cruise AV and the motorcycle. There were no injuries and police were not called.

A Cruise autonomous vehicle (“Cruise AV”), operating in autonomous mode, was proceeding westbound on Eddy Street at the intersection with Leavenworth Street when another vehicle made contact with the center rear bumper of the Cruise AV, damaging the Cruise AV’s left center rear bumper and radar connector. Police were not called and no injuries were reported at the scene by either party. Both of the Cruise AV testers sitting in passenger seats later sought medical attention for neck stiffness.

On March 12, 2019 at approximately 4:07 pm, a Lyft Autonomous Vehicle ("Lyft AV"), operating at full manual mode, made contact at approximately 2 mph with a parked 3rd party vehicle while reversing during a multi-point turn. There was no driver or passenger present in the 3rd party vehicle. The incident occurred on Pettis Avenue near El Camino Boulevard in Mountain View, CA. Minor damage is limited to the left rear bumper area of the Lyft AV (A010) and the left rear driver's side of the 3rd party, pending further inspection. The owner of the 3rd party vehicle came outside to exchange information with the operators. No injuries were reported and the police were not notified.

The subject Mercedes-Benz DRIVE PILOT test vehicle was traveling between 15 – 20 mph in the #2 northbound lane on the 605 Freeway in California in stop and go traffic with the L3 ADS activated by the driver. The vehicle’s ADS determined that a truck traveling in the adjacent lane had a trajectory towards the Drive Pilot’s lane, and so the Mercedes-Benz test vehicle autonomously applied the brakes to avoid a collision. After applying the brakes and bringing itself to a standstill, the Mercedes-Benz was then struck in the rear bumper by a trailing semi-truck that did not stop in time. No injuries were reported, no airbags deployed in either vehicle, and both vehicles were able to be driven from the scene of the incident. The Mercedes-Benz vehicle experienced minor damage to the rear bumper, and no damage was observed on the semi-truck at the scene. The CA Traffic Collision Report for the subject incident noted a violation of California Vehicle Code 22350 (unsafe speed for traffic conditions) by the semi-truck in the #2 lane that struck the rear bumper of the Mercedes-Benz.

The subject Mercedes-Benz vehicle was driving in stop and go traffic on the 405 south freeway in Gardena, California with the L3 ADS activated. The test route selected by the driver in the vehicle's navigation system indicated an upcoming exit, so the driver began to prepare for a lane change towards the highway exit by deactivating the L3 ADS and activating the turn signal. Once the vehicle was in conventional driving mode, the driver looked for a gap in the adjacent lane to merge towards the exit lane, applied the brakes, and slowed the vehicle down. The SUV following the Mercedes-Benz vehicle did not respond in time to the vehicle's braking and contacted the rear of the Mercedes-Benz approximately 10 seconds after the L3 ADS was deactivated. The Mercedes-Benz vehicle experienced minor damage to the rear bumper. No injuries were reported, no airbags deployed in either vehicle, and both vehicles were driven from the scene of the incident.

The Mercedes-Benz vehicle was traveling NB on Highway 280, near Bird Avenue, in lane one. Traffic ahead began slowing, and the operator attempted a right lane change into lane two. The Mercedes-Benz vehicle operator was unable to complete the lane change and instead applied the brakes. The Mercedes-Benz operator was unable to avoid contact with the Ford vehicle that was in front of it, and the Mercedes-Benz front bumper contacted the rear bumper of the Ford vehicle.

The Motional vehicle was traveling on 4th Ave, between Brooks Ct and Broadway St, in Venice, CA in manual mode in the sole northbound lane. While navigating the narrow two-lane, unstriped road, the safety driver slowed the vehicle to 1.5mph to allow a driver coming in the opposite direction to navigate past the Motional vehicle. The other vehicle’s driver side wing mirror made contact with the Motional vehicle’s driver side wing mirror and LIDAR casing, causing cosmetic damage. The safety driver pulled the vehicle to the side of the road and exchanged information with the driver of the other vehicle. There was one other vehicle involved, minor cosmetic damage to the Motional vehicle, minor cosmetic damage to the third-party vehicle, and no injuries occurred due to the incident.

On Wednesday, May 22, 2024 at approximately 3:45pm PST, a Nuro Prius operating in manual mode bumped a pedestrian at the intersection of Webster Street and Middlefield Road in Palo Alto, California. The Nuro Prius was in autonomous mode when it approached the intersection and came to a stop at the stop bar on Webster Street. It is a two-way stop with the traffic on Middlefield having right of way. The Nuro Prius nudged forward due to an occlusion.The Nuro operator judged the nudging to be too far and disengaged autonomous mode to reverse in manual. When reversing, the operator bumped a pedestrian crossing the street behind the Nuro Prius. The pedestrian was not injured and after speaking with the operator, left the scene without providing additional information. There was no damage to the vehicle and law enforcement was not involved.

On Wednesday, January 31st at approximately 4:20pm, a Nuro Prius was operating in autonomous mode driving south on Boyce Ave in Palo Alto. As the Prius proceeded straight through the intersection of Boyce Ave. and Fife Ave. a Honda CR-V ran the Fife Ave. stop sign and initiated a left turn. The Honda CR-V rear-ended the Nuro Prius, though the Nuro driver took control of the Prius and nudged right in an attempt to avoid impact. Both vehicles sustained de minimis damage. Law enforcement was not involved and there were no injuries reported or VRUs present.

The Pony.ai autonomous vehicle ("Pony.ai AV") was stopped for approximately 3 minutes at the red light in the far right lane on Milmont Dr. preparing to turn right onto Dixon Landing Rd. In front of the Pony.ai AV are several other vehicles also preparing to turn right. While stopped, Vehicle 2 came up quickly immediately behind the Pony.ai AV then proceeded to stop abruptly. Vehicle 2 then proceeds to creep up towards the Pony.ai with the driver of Vehicle 2 appearing to look down. Vehicle 2 then lurches forward quickly towards the Pony.ai AV. The Pony.ai AV operator proceeded to disengage from autonomous mode to attempt to avoid an accident, however, as the Pony.ai AV vehicle operator attempted to step on the throttle, the Pony.ai AV is rear-ended by Vehicle 2. The Pony.ai AV was stopped at 0 mph, while the approximate speed of Vehicle 2 at the point of collision was 5 mph. The Pony.ai AV operator noted that prior to the collision, the driver of Vehicle 2 appeared to drive erratically across other intersections as well. The contact between the vehicles caused a moderate damage to the back of the Pony.ai AV and moderate damage to Vehicle 2. Both drivers pulled over to the side of the roadway and exchanged information. There were no injuries reported and the police were not called. Pursuant to protocol, Pony.ai ran simulations after the accident to determine if the ADV would have reacted differently. The results indicate the Pony.ai ADV would not have reacted differently.

On August 21, 2025 at 12:59 AM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in Los Angeles, California was in a collision involving a shopping cart on E. 11th Street near Imperial Street. The Waymo AV was traveling northwestbound on E. 11th Street when a pedestrian standing in the roadway on the south side of E. 11th Street pushed a shopping cart towards the Waymo AV’s lane of travel. The shopping cart made contact with the left side of the Waymo AV. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode. The Waymo AV sustained damage.

On March 22, 2024 at 10:00 PM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle ("Waymo AV") operating in San Francisco, California was in a collision involving a passenger car near the 200 block of Church Street before Market Street. The Waymo AV was traveling north on Church Street towards the intersection with Market Street when it came to a stop behind an SUV which was stopped in-lane to load passengers. Another SUV approached from behind the Waymo AV and came to a stop. The lead SUV finished loading passengers and proceeded forward to the stop line at Market Street, and the Waymo AV proceeded forward as well. The trailing SUV proceeded forward and the front of the SUV made contact with the rear of the Waymo AV. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV's Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode. The Waymo AV sustained damage and the SUV left the scene.

On July 11, 2023 at 10:13 AM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in San Francisco, California was in a collision involving a passenger vehicle on Martin Avenue at Mullen Avenue. While completing a right turn from Martin Avenue onto Mullen Avenue in autonomous mode, the Waymo AV slowed to a stop while entering a narrow roadway. As the Waymo AV started to slowly proceed forward, the test driver transitioned the vehicle to manual mode and proceeded forward, making contact with a parked passenger vehicle. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was not engaged and a test driver was operating the Waymo AV in manual mode. Both vehicles sustained damage.

On August 30, 2024 at 10:57 AM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in Los Angeles, California was in a collision involving an SUV on Highland Avenue at Beverly Boulevard. The Waymo AV was traveling in the leftmost of the two southbound lanes on Highland Avenue when it began to brake to yield to stopped traffic ahead. Simultaneously, an SUV that was previously in the right lane changed lanes and approached the Waymo AV closely from behind. As the Waymo AV continued to slow, the SUV made contact with the rear of the Waymo AV. The SUV then reversed, drove across the curbed, grass median, and proceeded to travel north on Highland Avenue. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode, and a test driver was present (in the driver’s seating position). Both vehicles sustained damage.

On September 18, 2024 at 8:44 PM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle ("Waymo AV") operating in San Francisco, California was in a collision involving a van on Potrero Avenue at 16th Street. The Waymo AV was stopped in a queue of traffic in the leftmost of two through lanes on southbound Potrero Avenue at the intersection with 16th Street when a van traveling behind the Waymo AV passed the Waymo AV on the left to enter the dedicated left turn lane. The passenger side of the van made contact with the rear left sensor of the Waymo AV. Without stopping, the van then crossed the double yellow line to the northbound side of Potrero Avenue, turned left onto eastbound 16th Street, and left the scene. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV's Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode, and a test driver was present (in the driver's seating position). The Waymo AV sustained damage to the rear left sensor housing and assembly.

On December 2, 2024 at 10:54 AM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in Los Angeles, California was in a collision involving a plastic crate on East 3rd Street at South Central Avenue. The Waymo AV was traveling westbound in the center lane on East 3rd Street, crossing the intersection with South Central Avenue when the front passenger side of the Waymo AV made contact with a plastic crate that was in the roadway within the Waymo AV’s lane of travel. The contact with the Waymo AV caused the crate to move into the adjacent right lane, which was occupied by a scooterist. The front tire of the scooter made contact with the crate and the scooter and scooterist fell. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode. Given the speed at which the scooter was traveling at the time of the contact, the scooter may have sustained damage.

On December 25, 2024 at 8:40 AM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in San Francisco, California was in a collision involving a passenger car on Broadway near Buchanan Street. The Waymo AV was parked at the curb in the westbound direction of Broadway street, in front of a parked passenger car, when another passenger car parallel parked in front of the Waymo AV within close proximity to the front of the Waymo AV. Due to the proximity of the now parked passenger car in front of the Waymo AV, the Waymo AV was unable to unpark from the curb, and the ADS was disengaged to maneuver the Waymo AV away from the curb. The Waymo AV was maneuvered in manual mode to unpark from the curb. During this maneuver, the test driver reversed the Waymo AV and the rear of the Waymo AV made contact with the front of the passenger car that was parked behind the Waymo AV. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was not engaged and a test driver was operating the Waymo AV in conventional mode. Both vehicles sustained damage.

On December 25, 2025 at 4:08 AM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in San Francisco, California was in a collision involving a fallen utility line on 23rd Street near Rhode Island Street. The Waymo AV was traveling eastbound on 23rd Street when the front of the Waymo AV made contact with a fallen utility line hanging in the travel lane. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode. The utility line sustained damage.

On January 29, 2026 at 9:00 AM PT a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in Los Angeles, California was in a collision involving an SUV on W. Pico Boulevard near S. Sepulveda Boulevard. The Waymo AV was stopped facing northeast on W. Pico Boulevard in the second from the right lane in a queue of traffic for a red light at the intersection with S. Sepulveda Boulevard when a pedestrian approached the stationary Waymo AV and made contact with the front right sensor, causing the Waymo AV to remain stopped in lane. While the Waymo AV was stopped, an SUV that was stopped directly behind the Waymo AV proceeded to change lanes to the left lane and the right side of the SUV made contact with the rear left side of the stationary Waymo AV. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode. Both vehicles sustained damage.

On February 15, 2023 at 5:43 AM PST a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in San Francisco, California was in a collision involving road debris on North Point Street at Buchanan Street. The Waymo AV was proceeding East on North Point Street through the intersection with Buchanan Street when the front of the Waymo AV made contact with cardboard debris. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was engaged in autonomous mode. The Waymo AV sustained damage.

On July 12, 2021 at 3:10 PM PDT, a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) was in a collision involving a van at Broadway and Gough Street in San Francisco. The Waymo AV, while in autonomous mode, was waiting to make a left turn and yielding to oncoming traffic, when the test driver (in the driver’s seating position) transitioned to manual mode and proceeded with a left turn manually. During the left turn, an approaching van struck the right side of the Waymo AV. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV was in manual mode.

A Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in San Francisco, California was in a collision involving a parked vehicle on the 200 block of Parnassus Avenue. While operating in manual mode, the operator of the Waymo vehicle was attempting to enter the adjacent travel lane from a parallel parked position on the right-hand edge of the street, when they made contact with the rear of a vehicle parked directly in front of the Waymo vehicle. The Waymo vehicle sustained minor damage to the front bumper and sensor casing. The other party’s vehicle sustained minor scratches and denting to the rear bumper.

On August 16th, 2022 at 9:12 AM PST a Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) operating in San Francisco, California was in a collision involving a passenger vehicle on Broadway at Sansome Street. The Waymo AV was stopped behind a bus in the right lane, facing East on Broadway. The passenger car that had been stopped behind the Waymo AV began moving forward. The front of the passenger car made contact with the rear of the Waymo AV. The Waymo AV sustained minor damage. At the time of the impact, the Waymo AV’s Level 4 ADS was not engaged and a test driver was operating the Waymo AV in manual mode.

A Waymo Autonomous Vehicle (“Waymo AV”) was traveling northbound on 3rd Street in San Francisco in manual mode when it was rear-ended. The Waymo AV was traveling in autonomous mode at approximately 30 MPH in the leftmost lane as it approached the intersection at 24th Street. In this location there are traffic pylons on the left edge of the leftmost lane that separate this lane from the municipal tram line that operates in the median of 3rd Street. As the Waymo AV approached the intersection, a San Francisco MUNI city bus traveling at approximately 40 MPH in the right adjacent lane began to overtake the Waymo AV from the right, while moving toward the Waymo’s lane of travel. Due to the encroaching city bus and the pylons on the left edge of the Waymo AV’s lane, the Waymo AV began to brake. The Waymo AV test driver disengaged autonomous mode and took control of the Waymo AV. Approximately 1 second later, the passenger vehicle behind the Waymo AV made contact with the Waymo AV’s rear bumper at approximately 27 MPH. The Waymo AV was traveling approximately 4 MPH. The Waymo AV sustained significant damage to its rear bumper, and the passenger vehicle sustained significant damage to its front bumper. The driver of the passenger vehicle and the Waymo AV test driver were transported to receive medical attention. The Waymo AV co-driver reported minor injuries but did not receive medical attention. Amended Sections 3 and 4.

On November 27th at 1:27pm, Car 1 (weride av) - while in autonomous mode - was making a legal, protected, left turn from Coleman Ave. Car 1, turning onto W Hedding St., performed the turn from the second lane from the left and was travelling 11 mph when Car 1 then slowed down while still in the intersection. It is at this time Car 1's safety driver disengaged Car 1 from autonomous mode by using the throttle; this put car 1 into manual mode. It is at this time when car 2 (Ford f-150 XLT), traveling at 18 mph and also making a left turn from Coleman Ave within the same lane as car 1, struck and rear ended car 1 while both cars were still in the intersection. Car 1 sustained minor damage to its rear bumper and car 2 sustained minor damage to front bumper. Both parties pulled over to exchange information. Car 2 did not provide Registration and Insurance for their respective car. Car 2's driver did give us driver's license information but the driver of the vehicle (car 2) at the time of the incident was a different person than that represented on the driver's license presented.

An unoccupied Zoox autonomous vehicle was traveling east on Hill Street toward Valencia Street in San Francisco when an SUV (Vehicle 2) that had been stationary while in an apparent attempt to parallel park along the right curb suddenly pulled out into the path of the approaching Zoox vehicle. The Zoox vehicle braked hard and attempted to steer left, but the right front wheel and body panel of the Zoox vehicle made contact with the left front wheel and panel of Vehicle 2. The Zoox vehicle was towed from the scene for inspection and was found to have sustained minor damage. There were no reported injuries, and police were not notified

Zoox OL-316 Attachment Crash description for the Zoox incident that occurred on 4/4/2025 in the intersection of 11th and Bryant Streets in San Francisco: An unoccupied Zoox vehicle in autonomy was stopped at a red light in the right travel lane on southbound 11th Street at the intersection with Bryant and Division Streets in San Francisco. At that time, a cyclist on an eBike came to a stop in the bike lane to the right of the Zoox vehicle. The cyclist began to proceed before the light turned green and headed straight. After the light turned green, the Zoox vehicle proceeded straight towards Bryant Street. While nearly through the intersection, the cyclist abruptly veered left into the path of the Zoox vehicle and accelerated toward the front of the Zoox vehicle in violation of a red crosswalk signal and in violation of the Zoox vehicle’s right-of-way. The Zoox vehicle appropriately braked hard in response to the cyclist's maneuver, but contact was unavoidable. The eBike laterally impacted the Zoox vehicle’s right front fender and body side, then the cyclist impacted the right front body of the Zoox vehicle. The Zoox vehicle then came to a full stop. The cyclist then rode over to the sidewalk and remained briefly stopped on the sidewalk before getting back on the eBike and riding away. The Zoox vehicle cleared the intersection, then pulled over on Bryant Street, and shortly after was towed from the scene for inspection. The Zoox vehicle sustained minor damage to the right front body. The police were not called. No injuries were reported nor apparent with the cyclist.

An unoccupied Zoox vehicle (Vehicle 1) was traveling east on 13th Street approaching Bryant Street in San Francisco when it was changing lanes from the right lane to the middle lane with its left turn signal activated. An SUV (Vehicle 2), also traveling in the same direction in the left lane, started to change course to the right towards the middle lane. The right front corner of the SUV struck the left rear of the Zoox vehicle. The Zoox vehicle came to a stop after the collision. Shortly after, the Zoox vehicle turned left onto Bryant Street, as did Vehicle 2. The Zoox vehicle then pulled over on Bryant Street, but the Vehicle 2 driver did not stop to exchange information. The Zoox vehicle was found to have sustained minor damage to the left rear wheel. Police were not called, and no injuries were reported.

An occupied Zoox autonomous vehicle (Vehicle 1) was traveling west on Duboce Avenue past Otis Street when it encountered debris in the lane. The Zoox vehicle braked hard for the debris and was then rear ended by a close-following Pickup (Vehicle 2) that was abruptly merging into the lane directly behind the Zoox vehicle. The Vehicle 2 driver then reversed and left the scene without attempting to exchange information. Shortly after, the Zoox vehicle cleared the scene, turned right onto Valencia Street, and pulled over to allow the riders to exit the vehicle. The Zoox vehicle then returned to base for inspection and was found to have sustained moderate damage. There were no reported injuries, and the police were notified.

A Zoox vehicle in autonomy had made a right turn from Oakdell Rd. onto Santa Cruz Ave. in Menlo Park, CA and was preparing to make an immediate, unprotected left turn onto Sharon Road. The Zoox vehicle was slowing and moving at approximately 2 mph with its brake lamps and left turn indicator illuminated, yielding to an oncoming vehicle with the right of way. A following vehicle - traveling at approximately 24 mph - then struck the Zoox vehicle's right rear bumper, and that vehicle's driver airbag appeared to have deployed on impact. The Zoox operator disengaged autonomy, proceeded with the left turn, and pulled over. The following vehicle continued its path of travel, veered out of the lane, and collided with a tree on the left side of the road. The Menlo Park Police Department was called to the scene. Two Zoox operators sustained minor injuries and it is unknown if the driver of the other vehicle sustained injuries.

A Zoox vehicle in manual mode was stopped at the intersection of Vallejo Street and Sansome Street when a following vehicle made contact with the rear sensor array resulting in minor damage to the sensor bracket. No injuries were reported and the police were not called to the scene.

A Zoox vehicle was making a right lane change in manual mode on Folsom St between 4th and Mahini St., when a passenger vehicle continuing straight made contact with the left rear bumper of the Zoox vehicle. There were no injuries and police were not called.

A Zoox vehicle was proceeding straight in autonomy through an intersection with a green light and right of way when vehicle 2 attempted an illegal left turn across lanes of traffic into Zoox’s right of way. The safety driver disengaged and applied max braking effort which allowed Zoox to mitigate but not completely prevent the unavoidable collision. The Zoox vehicle struck the right front corner of vehicle 2. No injuries were reported and the police were not called to the scene.
